front: Definition of a relation from A to B
back: A relation R from A to B is a subset of A × B. We write a R b when (a, b) ∈ R.
A relation R on A with no ordered pairs at all: R = ∅ ⊂ A × A.
A relation R on A containing every ordered pair: R = A × A.
R is reflexive on A if (a, a) ∈ R for every a ∈ A.
R is symmetric if (a₁, a₂) ∈ R implies (a₂, a₁) ∈ R for all a₁, a₂ ∈ A.
R is transitive if (a₁, a₂) ∈ R and (a₂, a₃) ∈ R imply (a₁, a₃) ∈ R for all a₁, a₂, a₃ ∈ A.
A relation that is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. Every equivalence relation partitions its set into disjoint classes.
f : A → B is one-one if f(a₁) = f(a₂) implies a₁ = a₂ — different inputs give different outputs.
f : A → B is onto if every element of B is the image of at least one element of A, i.e. range(f) = B.
A function that is both one-one and onto. Bijections are exactly the invertible functions.
For f : A → B and g : B → C, the composite is (g ∘ f)(x) = g(f(x)), a function from A to C.
If f : X → Y is bijective, its inverse f⁻¹ : Y → X satisfies f⁻¹(y) = x exactly when f(x) = y. Then f⁻¹ ∘ f = I_X and f ∘ f⁻¹ = I_Y.
f is invertible if and only if f is bijective (one-one and onto).

front: Number of one-one functions from a set of m elements to a set of n elements
back: If n ≥ m, it is n(n − 1)(n − 2)⋯(n − m + 1); it is 0 when n < m.
f = g when they have the same domain and codomain, and f(x) = g(x) for every x in the domain.
I_A = {(a, a) : a ∈ A} is the identity relation on A; I_A(x) = x is the corresponding identity function on A.

front: How many equivalence relations on a 3-element set?
back: 5 — one for each partition of a 3-element set (Bell number B₃ = 5).

front: Relation R = {(a, b) : a − b is an integer} on R
back: An equivalence relation: reflexive (a − a = 0), symmetric (−(a − b) is an integer) and transitive (sum of integers is an integer).

front: Relation of congruence modulo 5 on Z
back: R = {(a, b) : 5 divides (a − b)} is an equivalence relation; its classes are the five residue classes 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 mod 5.

front: Subset relation on a power set
back: R = {(A, B) : A ⊆ B} on P(X) is reflexive and transitive but not symmetric, so it is not an equivalence relation.
